decisions.executionNote: Approach basket with left arm, gradually rolling gripper to straddle handle vertically. Board appears to specify a white cup with tan band; right arm stays clear.
Finish rolling left fingers vertically and advance toward the moving basket handle, tracking its rightward conveyor drift.
Align left jaw gap with the handle crown using head geometry; keep vertical finger closure and follow the basket's rightward motion.
Shift left wrist toward visible handle crown without further forward push; refine alignment before closing.
Close around the nearby handle segment and begin a short upward retention test; verify basket motion visually before a full lift.
Basket did not follow the test lift. Reopen and move farther forward and lower to place the handle inside, rather than ahead of, the finger gap.
The handle now intersects the open jaw region in the left wrist view. Lower slightly, seat the grasp, then close while matching belt motion.
Lift the closed left grasp by 10 cm, with a small leftward motion to test visible basket retention and restore left-side clearance.
Basket was not retained and has entered the right workspace. Withdraw left arm safely; prepare right arm to grasp the basket without crossing arms.
Correct the rejected tensor; small right-arm approach and roll, left withdrawal, both starting from the unchanged observation.
Move right gripper toward the approaching handle crown while finishing vertical jaw alignment; left arm clears to its own side.
Advance right fingers toward the center of the arch, using the visible wrist handle to correct lateral alignment; leave jaws open.
Seat the right gripper farther around the handle crown and correct leftward alignment, then close while tracking conveyor drift.
Finish right-handle closure, then lift 9.6 cm and inspect whether the basket follows. The white tan-banded cup is now entering from the left.
Horizontal grasp again missed. Reorient right gripper downward above the front basket rim for a vertical rim grasp, avoiding further forward pushing.
Reduce orientation increment following the zero-step continuity rejection; prepare a top-down rim grasp.
Continue right top-down orientation above the front rim. Prepare left arm high above the tan-banded cup while keeping the workspaces separate.
Replan from executed prefix with reduced right rotation and gradual descent. Left approaches above the cup, not contacting it before basket lift.
Bring right fingertips downward onto the front rim with jaws closing fore-aft. Align left above the image-matched cup while keeping it ungrasped until basket is lifted.
Near rim approach is kinematically cramped. Move right wrist forward and higher toward the handle, relieving wrist fold before descending. Continue left cup alignment overhead.
Use fixed right orientation and a small downward/retracted approach to regain feasible motion, following the front rim laterally. Left remains open above the cup.
Right fingertips are level with the front rim; adjust toward its outside and close around the lip. Keep left cup approach open until a confirmed basket lift.
Test the front-rim grasp with an 8.6 cm right-arm lift. Left remains open and tracks the tan-banded cup without picking it yet.
Basket visibly followed the right rim grasp. Add height margin while lowering the left open jaws toward the board-matched white cup with brown band.
Hold the lifted basket steady. Lower left fingers around the cup body, track its motion, and close for a pickup.
Complete cup closure and lift it 8.8 cm to test retention visually, keeping the already lifted basket steady in the right hand.
Cup did not remain between the closed fingers. Reopen, track rightward to its center, and descend to grasp the body rather than the rim edge; basket stays lifted.
Wrist view shows cup offset toward the far side of the jaw gap. Center farther forward while matching belt drift, reseat at body height, and close.
Finish closing on the centered cup, then make a small upward-and-back retention test while holding the basket above the conveyor.
Cup is visibly retained. Lift and bring it inward with the left arm while bringing the elevated basket inward on the right, preserving arm separation and grasp closure.
Raise retained cup with a retracted path for reach margin. Move basket toward the midline while keeping right wrist on its own side and both grasps closed.
After the guarded prefix, reduce left wrist downward pitch to regain reach and raise cup clearance. Gently level the held basket and bring it nearer the center without crossing wrists.
Bring the retained cup above the basket's left interior, gaining vertical clearance with mild wrist tilt. Keep right wrist positive and left wrist negative at the midline.
Regain right-arm reach margin by retracting and easing pitch after the guard. Advance the cup above the opening, with wrists separated fore-aft and on their own sides.
Use much smaller right wrist relief increments after zero-step rejection. Maintain both grasps while moving cup slowly above the opening.
Reduce extension rather than forcing upward reach. Aim the retained cup inward with a gentle yaw while moving basket slightly back and keeping both wrists on their own sides.
Aim the cup farther over the basket opening using yaw, not arm crossing. Slight left retraction preserves wrist clearance; right maintains the lifted rim grasp.
Separate the left wrist forward from the right wrist to relieve observed contact error, while carrying the cup above the basket's far-left interior. Keep basket stationary and lifted.
Left forward reach reached a continuity limit. Hold the cup still and gently yaw the basket about its offset rim grasp to bring the opening underneath, without crossing wrists.
Aim the cup a little farther into the left portion of the lifted basket, then open the left gripper to deposit it. Keep the basket grasp closed and inspect the fall.
Withdraw the open left gripper for a clear view and allow the released cup to settle. Maintain the basket's elevated right-hand grasp.
Retry open-left withdrawal with much smaller increments after the zero-step continuity rejection; keep elevated basket stationary.
The tan-banded cup is visibly inside the basket. Add basket height margin with a slow upward-and-back lift while clearing the open left arm.
Cup remains visible inside the basket. Keep right grasp and basket height steady while withdrawing the left arm fully to eliminate nearby contact and let the cup settle.
